standing: Discriminating negative controls over the exported positive Run. TAMPERED-RESULT controls remint every enclosing identity and preserve citation membership, so only semantic replay can refuse them. IDENTITY/RETENTION controls are refused at retained-closure admission, before replay. Neither family is a future-authentication claim.

identityAndRetentionControls.description: One byte inside the retained run3 H preimage frame is flipped while the CAS key is left alone: the stored bytes no longer re-hash to the key.
identityAndRetentionControls.target: run3 frame byte flipped, key unchanged
identityAndRetentionControls.masksLater: Yes -- this retained-closure refusal precedes semantic proof replay entirely; the replay comparison is never reached.

identityAndRetentionControls.description: The Plan still DECLARES policyDigest but the PolicyDocumentV2 preimage bytes are not retained. A digest declaration alone never retains its bytes.
identityAndRetentionControls.masksLater: Yes -- this retained-closure refusal precedes semantic proof replay entirely; the replay comparison is never reached.

identityAndRetentionControls.description: Different bytes are stored under the policy digest, so the fetched preimage does not re-hash to the digest that named it.
identityAndRetentionControls.target: policy preimage replaced with other bytes under the same key
identityAndRetentionControls.masksLater: Yes -- this retained-closure refusal precedes semantic proof replay entirely; the replay comparison is never reached.

identityAndRetentionControls.description: The Plan preimage is re-framed under a domain that no domain set registers, and is stored under its own correct digest so the rehash check passes. Frame admission requires the domain to be a member of the annotation's named set.
identityAndRetentionControls.target: plan preimage re-framed under domain "plan.v3-unregistered", stored under its OWN digest, and run.planId repointed with run3 reminted
identityAndRetentionControls.masksLater: No -- the frame is stored under its own correct digest, so the PREIMAGE_REHASH_MISMATCH check passes and the frame-domain check is the first refusal. Compare the same-key variant below, where the rehash check fires first and masks this one.

identityAndRetentionControls.description: Same fault written in place under the original key. Recorded to show the MASKING explicitly: the CAS rehash check refuses first and the frame-domain check is never reached.
identityAndRetentionControls.target: plan frame re-framed in place, CAS key left unchanged
identityAndRetentionControls.masksLater: Yes -- PREIMAGE_REHASH_MISMATCH fires first and masks the FRAME_DOMAIN_UNREGISTERED check this case was written to exercise.

identityAndRetentionControls.description: C(X) is offered where the annotation says h-identity, under its own correct raw digest. C(X) does not begin with the framing prefix and SHA256(C(X)) is not H(D,X), so it fails the prefix.
identityAndRetentionControls.target: C(snapshot) stored under SHA256(C(snapshot)) and run.snapshotId repointed at it, with run3 reminted
identityAndRetentionControls.masksLater: No -- the payload is stored under its own correct digest, so the rehash check passes and the FRAME_PREFIX check is the first refusal.

identityAndRetentionControls.description: A well-formed, hash-valid fact2 that belongs to no evaluated view is cited from a finding. identity section 3: "A well-formed, hash-valid object outside this closure is refused, rather than admitted as hidden finding evidence."
identityAndRetentionControls.target: a hash-valid fact2 outside every evaluated view cited from a finding, with the finding and every enclosing identity reminted
identityAndRetentionControls.masksLater: No -- the graph is fully reminted and internally hash-consistent, so every digest and frame check passes; the citation-closure join is the first refusal.
